title: PR #313 · the woodwork sheet is a menu
blurb: The woodwork sheet becomes a menu: the species is resolved in one place, an entry nobody selects is never fetched, and the shelf says what it resolved. Two entry points reach that work — the first paint of the shelf, and an apply from the debug panel — so this is one change on two sheets, sharing one node map. Read either sheet's effects ledger against the PR's own request table.

The fibre rides the SAME UVs the figure does. Laid by the module's default constant it is 4.8x wrong under sapele — with every whole-frame number still in the normal range. #297's crossed-fibre defect, one surface over.
Five report lists. applied / needsRebuild / needsReload / refused are transitions; resolved is a statement.

steps.aside: not applied and not asked for — but still reported, so a fibre that never bound says so on every apply after the one that discovered it

steps.label: readback
steps.aside: resolved from `next`, NOT read off woodwork.resolved — the two differ exactly when a species change is waiting for a rebuild, and a typo has to reach the report when the value is set rather than one rebuild later

steps.expr: ({ applied, needsRebuild, refused: refused.concat(readBack.refused), resolved: readBack.resolved })

steps.comment: Compared AFTER resolution, never as raw strings: everything off-roster resolves to the default, so walnut and rosewood name one shelf. Comparing the requests would offer a rebuild for a change a rebuild cannot make.
Pure, and in a module with no Three.js in it, so G54 can assert on it without a WebGL context.

steps.name: waiting
steps.expr: wanted.species === built ? '' : ' — built with ' + built + ', rebuild to change it'

steps.name: lines
steps.expr: ['woodwork sheet: ' + wanted.species + ' (' + sheet + ')' + waiting, 'wood fibre: ' + fibreInForce + (fibreInForce === fibreAsked ? '' : ' (asked for ' + fibreAsked + ')')]
steps.aside: G54's first draft matched the species by bare substring and was green on a read-back naming no species at all — rosewood and sapele each appear inside their own URL. Anchoring to `woodwork sheet: <name> (` reddened six clauses.

graphs.title: first paint
graphs.blurb: The woodwork slice of buildShelf, as it stands after #313. The species is resolved here and nowhere else, which is the whole of the menu's laziness: an entry nobody selects is never fetched. Read the effects ledger against the PR's own request table. Flip Layer to Tests and exactly two nodes move: bindSheet and applyWoodFibre each take a parameter with a real default, so a double goes in at the call. fibreMapFor keeps canvas 2d, because it has no seam and no vitest spec reaches it — only smoke:render does, in a real browser with nothing substituted.

graphs.title: panel apply
graphs.blurb: The other half of #313: the woodwork slice of applySettings, and the fifth ApplyReport category it earned. The other four are all transitions, and a transition cannot describe a configuration that was wrong from the first frame — so `resolved` states rather than diffs, on every apply, whether or not anything moved.
